---
title: Join Us
---

We welcome collaborators and applicants interested in **AI-enabled multi-hazard forecasting,
early warning systems, and decision support**.

Our work combines machine learning, physical modelling, and uncertainty analysis to support
risk-informed decisions for natural hazards.

## Opportunities

### TREES DLA PhD projects — 2027 entry

Applications are open through the **TREES Doctoral Landscape Award**. The application deadline is **14 December 2026 at 17:00 UK time**.

```{=html}
<div class="resource-grid">
  <article class="resource-card">
    <p class="resource-type">PhD · CASE partnership with BGS</p>
    <h3>Quantifying Landslide Impacts across Europe using AI</h3>
    <p>Develop AI and Earth observation methods to map landslides across Europe and investigate their contribution to disaster impacts and multi-hazard risk.</p>
    <p><strong>Supervisors:</strong> Faith Taylor and Lorenzo Nava, King’s College London.<br><strong>Co-supervisors:</strong> Alessandro Novellino and Ekbal Hussain, British Geological Survey (BGS). Includes a BGS placement of at least three months.</p>
    <div class="resource-links"><a href="https://www.trees-dla.ac.uk/projects/quantifying-landslide-impacts-across-europe-using-ai">Official project description ↗</a></div>
  </article>
  <article class="resource-card">
    <p class="resource-type">PhD · AI and cascading hazards</p>
    <h3>Predicting Extreme Geohazard Flows with AI</h3>
    <p>Combine satellite, terrain, seismic and environmental data to reconstruct and predict long-runout flows, including debris flows and glacial lake outburst floods.</p>
    <p><strong>Supervisors:</strong> Tom Matthews and Lorenzo Nava, King’s College London.<br><strong>Co-supervisor:</strong> Max Van Wyk de Vries, University of Cambridge.</p>
    <div class="resource-links"><a href="https://www.trees-dla.ac.uk/projects/predicting-extreme-geohazard-flows-ai">Official project description ↗</a></div>
  </article>
</div>
```

**How to apply:** follow the [TREES application guidance](https://www.trees-dla.ac.uk/apply) for eligibility, funding arrangements and the application portal. Advertised projects use Route 1; applicants can select up to three projects. Studentships are awarded through the TREES selection process.

TREES funding covers a stipend and UK-rate fees. A limited number of international studentships also cover overseas fees, subject to funding availability; consult the official guidance for the conditions that apply to you.

For project enquiries, email [lorenzo.nava@kcl.ac.uk](mailto:lorenzo.nava@kcl.ac.uk). Applications must be submitted through TREES.

## Research themes

- Multi-hazard and cascading event modelling
- Machine learning for hazard detection and forecasting
- Uncertainty-aware prediction and evaluation
- End-to-end warning pipelines and decision support
- Open tools, reproducible science, and real-world impact

## Further opportunities

For PhD, MSc, visiting research, and fellowship enquiries beyond the advertised projects above, please contact us using the guidance below.

### PhD / MSc students
Applicants with a strong quantitative background (e.g. machine learning, statistics, physics,
engineering, or geoscience) and an interest in hazards and resilience.

### Postdoctoral researchers
Researchers with evidence of independent work, strong writing, and a clear research agenda
aligned with the lab's themes.

## How to get in touch
